title: LLM Supplier Friction Index and Tactical Watchlist for Regulated Vertical Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a quantified Supplier Friction Index (SFI) and an actionable watchlist to inform procurement and runtime routing decisions for regulated-vertical customers (finance, healthcare, gov). The SFI combines technical compatibility, procurement/time-to-provision friction, licensing/regulatory risk, and operational fragility into a single, auditable score per model variant and region.

Why this matters: Customers in regulated verticals require predictable procurement timelines and clear signals for fallback readiness. Current sourcing signals focus on latency and cost but miss procurement lead time, license complexity, and regional availability windows. The SFI will bridge that gap and let PM, SRE, and Sales make informed tradeoffs when recommending dedicated vs hosted options.

Scope & Deliverables (two-week sprint):
- SFI rubric and scoring function (CSV + readme) that weights: latency percentiles, quantization compatibility score, hardware affinity score, license friction score, procurement lead time estimate, regional availability penalty, and model stability (time-to-fail signals).
- Prototype SFI dataset covering 30 candidate open models × 6 regions with sample scores and normalization.
- Tactical watchlist: top 10 low-friction models for fast-regulated rollouts and top 10 high-friction models requiring procurement or engineering investment.
- Dashboard mock (Console wireframe) showing per-model SFI, score breakdown, and recommended routing (hosted/dedicated/private) with procurement triggers.
- Signal pipeline spec: which telemetry events and external sources (model vendor updates, license changes, procurement tickets) will incrementally update SFI and emit alerts when scores cross thresholds.
- PRD summary for Sales enablement and procurement checklist.

Methodology & Data Sources:
- Latency & reliability: aggregates from runtime telemetry (trace percentiles by region, token-level error spikes) via ENG telemetry exports (ENG-1987).
- Quant compatibility: engineering compatibility matrix (ENG-2310) and internal quantization lab results.
- License & compliance: manual scoring from Legal + vendor docs; mapped to friction categories (open permissive / copyleft / restricted / commercial).
- Procurement lead time: historical ticket data + vendor SLA estimation.
- Regional availability: cloud marketplace and vendor region announcements.

Scoring example (prototype weights):
- Latency 25% (p50 normalized)
- Quant compatibility 20%
- License friction 20%
- Procurement lead time 15%
- Regional availability 10%
- Stability / observed degradation events 10%

Notes on trade-offs:
- Weighting will be validated against 6 historical enterprise rollouts; initial conservative bias towards license/procurement to favor predictable enterprise experiences.
- SFI intentionally blends technical and non-technical signals; we will maintain separate component scores for transparency.

Acceptance criteria:
- The SFI CSV and readme exist in Drive and include scores and component breakdown for at least 30 model/region combinations.
- Dashboard mock created and reviewed by Design and Solutions (review notes attached).
- Signal pipeline spec with a minimal event set that ENG can ingest (ENG-1987 referenced) and roadmap for automation.
- Sales/Procurement sign-off on the procurement lead time assumptions and license friction taxonomy.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: license nuances missed -> Mitigation: Legal workshop and sample clause mapping.
- Risk: telemetry gaps in some regions -> Mitigation: fall back to vendor-reported metrics with a confidence flag.

Next steps after MVP:
- Automate SFI computation via nightly job that refreshes dashboard and emits alerts into Slack/Console when a model's SFI changes by >10 points.
- Bind SFI thresholds to Canary/A/B rollout tooling so rollouts auto-evaluate model friction before switching traffic.
- Extend watchlist to include third-party vendor risk scores and procurement cost estimators.
